title: Stay risk-off as higher real yields and AI volatility threaten stocks: BofA
source_used: Investing.com (read on Yahoo Finance copy); Bloomberg (read on Yahoo Finance copy) for cross-check
key_facts: Investing.com, 16 Oct: Bank of America strategists led by Michael Hartnett 'continue to lean risk-off' for the next three to four weeks, citing 3% real yields, geopolitical risks, US midterm uncertainty and weak price action in AI-linked stocks.

They say the Fed needs to hike on 28 Oct 'to restore credibility', noting CPI has been above its 2% target for 66 consecutive months, and expect a hike to push long-end Treasury yields down about 20 basis points.
On AI, spenders and lenders are under pressure: private equity and business development company ETFs are back at 2026 lows and Oracle's credit default swaps are a stress point.
BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.4 from 8.1, ending the 'sell signal' triggered on 26 May.
The team is not adding tech: investors are the most overweight tech since August 2020 and an AI bubble in 2027 is 'now consensus'.

Bloomberg (Yahoo copy) says the note was published on 15 Oct and its call for an October hike is more hawkish than broad market pricing; swaps traders pared bets on a hike after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh did not dispel expectations of a hold.
quote_evidence: Bank of America strategists say they "continue to lean risk-off" (favouring safer assets) for the next three to four weeks, citing 3% real yields, geopolitical risks, midterm uncertainty, and weak price action in AI-linked stocks.
On the AI front, the strategists said spenders and lenders are under pressure.

Strategists led by Michael Hartnett said the Fed needs to hike on Oct. 28 and flagged oil and the U.S., Iran, Russia, and Ukraine situations as key risks, as well as the rising chance of a "wave-like" Democratic sweep in the midterms.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading bank's strategists tell clients to stay cautious on stocks as real yields and AI worries bite.
event_date: BofA note dated 15 Oct 2026 per Bloomberg; reported 16 Oct
